text:
lee: FYI I'm putting together a proposal for a heatmap-style sampling UI for fallback events during rollouts. need product + infra input.

maria: love the idea. want it to show by reason (timeout, OOM, model-mismatch) and by % of requests sampled.

ajay: critical: sampling must not change behavior or add latency. we should stream samples async to kafka/s3.

tess: UX idea: left sidebar cohort selector (model, route, customer tier), center heatmap time vs sampling rate, top control: live / historical toggle, slider for sample rate.

sam: would prefer an additional 'always-sample for flagged requests' checkbox so we can capture full traces for canaries.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollout v2.14 started 2026-02-10 08:21 UTC :rocket:

lee: example telemetry payload we'd expect:
```json
{
  "event": "fallback",
  "route_id": "/v1/complete",
  "model_variant": "redwood-std-q4",
  "fallback_reason": "timeout",
  "sampled": true,
  "trace_id": "abcd1234",
  "duration_ms": 1200
}
```

maria: good, also include customer_id (hashed) and decision_trace pointer.

ajay: infra: estimate cost impact? if we sample 0.5% of 1M rps that's a lot. prefer adaptive sampling: higher for new rollouts and errors.

tess: UX: heatmap intensity = sampled fallback count normalized by route traffic. hover drilldown -> list of sample traces with timeline and raw logs.

lee: audit needs: immutable export of sampled events for 90 days, with CSV/JSON download, and a replay API for offline playback.

sam: can we expose an API to set sampling policy per-customer? enterprise needs opt-in/opt-out for privacy regs.

ajay: ok that's doable; infra will need TTL and retention controls plus a cheap index for heatmap queries.

maria: one more: provide a 'replay to sandbox' button that replays a sample to a sandboxed runtime for root cause debugging.

lee: next steps: I'll draft a short spec with mockups. @ajay can you give rough SLO/cost numbers by EOD Friday? :eyes: 

ajay: yep, will ping with numbers.

tess: will mock screens on Monday and drop in figma link.

sam: +1, thanks all :thumbsup:
